title: 1 Move vs 5 Moves
summary: Martin gets five moves for every one of Tony's. It is simulated on a normal chess.com board: after each real move Tony makes four 'wasted' shuffle moves while Martin plays freely. Martin quickly wins material (knight, rook, queen); late on Tony reaches a king walk but Martin repeats Bf1-c4 while Tony shuffles, and the game ends in a threefold-repetition draw (~9:04).
rules: Bot makes 5 consecutive moves for every 1 player move (video simulated this with 4 player 'waiting' moves between real ones; a faithful remake should just give the bot 5 moves).
Whether a check ends the bot's sequence is not stated (in the video Tony's waiting moves had to answer checks).
Threefold repetition and other draw rules apply.
win_condition: Checkmate Martin (result in video: draw by repetition).
